title: Preserve captured subgraph dependencies in quantization graph utilities
body:
### Description

The quantization ONNXModel utilities only consider a node's explicit inputs. Values captured by an If or Loop subgraph are consequently missing from topological dependencies and unused-constant analysis. A valid model can be reordered so a capture precedes its producer, or lose a constant/initializer used only inside a subgraph.

Collect lexical dependencies recursively from GRAPH and GRAPHS attributes, including graph outputs that directly reference an outer value. Subtract each subgraph's formal inputs, dense/sparse initializers and local node outputs so local names correctly shadow outer values. Use this input set for both topological sorting and constant cleanup.

This addresses one missing-dependency problem in both consumers. It does not reorder subgraph-internal nodes or change the separate transformers.OnnxModel implementation.

### Validation

- Eight new unittest methods cover native If/Loop execution, nested captures, save/reload, captured constants and initializers, local-name shadowing, duplicate explicit inputs, and missing/cyclic capture rejection.
- The GRAPHS attribute control checks dependency ordering only; no custom operator execution is claimed.
- New and existing model graph tests: **11 methods passed, 9 subtests passed**.
- Restoring the original implementation produces **2 failing test methods and 9 failing subtests**, with 6 completed methods. Failures identify invalid ordering and removal of live captured values.
- Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed.

Exact-source native validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/onnxruntime/actions/runs/43401505086

The native runtime comes from the repository's official CPU Release build.py/CMake build at 8dea1194e974fa07b1d2f07a190949c3a92cab80. Its C++ sources match base a8246c0d094f1ab0d6bf236228e5e67683321cd7. The validation installs that built wheel and overlays the complete quantization package from this exact patch, verifying every Python file byte-for-byte and recording a SHA-256 manifest. Tests use normal native imports. This is targeted Linux CPU validation, not GPU execution or the full C++ suite.

### Motivation and Context

Control-flow subgraphs use ONNX lexical scoping. Graph transformations must retain and order those dependencies just as they do explicit node inputs.

novelty.same_root_cause: Subgraph lexical dependencies are missing from both model sorting and unused constant cleanup; addressed together as one improvement.
novelty.personal_history: No preexisting ONNX Runtime contribution; new task-created fork and independent source branch.

validation.lint: Ruff 0.12.12 check/format and git diff --check passed

limitations: Quantization ONNXModel external lexical dependencies only, not subgraph-internal sorting or transformers.OnnxModel.
Targeted Linux native CPU only; GRAPHS custom operator control is structural.
